drc.pooled_solo: On 27 June 2023, the Council unanimously extended the Group of Experts mandate to 1 August 2024. It requested a midterm report to the Council by 30 December 2023 and a final report by 15 June 2024. The Group shall send monthly updates to the Committee, except during the two report-due months.
drc.independent: On 27 June 2023, the UN Security Council unanimously adopted Resolution 2688 (2023), extending the Group of Experts mandate to 1 August 2024. A review for further extension was scheduled for 1 July 2024. The Council requested a midterm report to the Committee by 30 December 2023 and a final report by 15 June 2024.
drc.interactive: On 27 June 2023, the Council unanimously adopted Resolution 2688 (2023), extending the Group of Experts mandate to 1 August 2024. A review for further extension was scheduled for 1 July 2024. Experts must submit a midterm report to the Council by 30 December 2023 and a final report by 15 June 2024, accompanied by monthly updates.
drc.local_solo: On 27 June 2023, the UN Security Council unanimously adopted French draft S/2023/469 as Resolution 2688 (2023), with 15 votes in favour. The Council received the draft and adopted the resolution. No further reporting or review responsibilities were specified in the record.

unami.pooled_solo: On 30 May 2023, the Council adopted Resolution 2682 (2023), extending UNAMI's mandate to 31 May 2024. The Secretary-General was requested to report quarterly on UNAMI responsibilities and conduct an independent strategic review by 31 March 2024. This review must consult Iraq, UN agencies, Member States, regional organizations, independent experts, civil society, and Kuwait. Iraq's Government expressed support for the review in a letter dated 18 May
unami.independent: On 30 May 2023, the Council adopted Resolution 2682 (2023), extending UNAMI's mandate to 31 May 2024. The Secretary-General is requested to report on UNAMI's fulfilment of responsibilities every four months. The resolution mandates a UNAMI strategic review by 31 March 2024, requiring consultations with Iraq, UN agencies, Member States, regional bodies, experts, and civil society. Iraq's government expressed support.
